Answer: F
Reason: The chest X-ray shows elevation of the right hemidiaphragm and scalloping (irregular contour) of the left hemidiaphragm, which are characteristic radiographic signs of lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM), a systemic disorder involving abnormal smooth muscle proliferation in the thoracic and abdominal lymphatics. This condition explains the bilateral diaphragmatic abnormalities in a patient with respiratory symptoms like a persistent cold.
